bosses.name: The Ferryman of Shut Gates
bosses.mechanic: The ferryman charges a sluice pulse over two actions. An exposed valve can be interrupted by a marked hit or disruptor; failure leaves the party defending against the pulse. Its ordinary heavy strike follows the spent pulse.

phase.change: A damaged pump leaks: its ward shrinks by 3, but the next visible sluice pulse gains 2 damage. No extra action is granted.
phase.telegraph: The lantern goes out, yet the waterline keeps rising.

bosses.biography: A Rainward engineer built it to carry families across floodwater. During a siege the watch ordered it to shut the gates against arrivals, leaving the engineer's own household on the low bank. It still counts every empty boat as a failed rescue and opens the sluice whenever someone tries to pass without a passenger.
bosses.rumor: The empty ferry returns heavier than it left. One old boatwoman says its lantern last went out while someone was still calling from the low bank.

noncombatApproaches.label: Repair the pump and restart a rescue crossing
prerequisites: Find the engineer winch in the side workshop
survival 6 or a trained craft companion
noncombatApproaches.result: The ferry opens a safe crossing; keep the pump plan as route proof.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Local security rises; passage serves households before traders.

noncombatApproaches.label: Carry a stranded named household over
prerequisites: Meet the stranded household on the actual low bank
noncombatApproaches.result: A completed rescue satisfies the ferryman current command.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The ferryman permits your party through; it still refuses empty commercial crossings.

noncombatApproaches.label: Buy the watch command and sell priority passage
noncombatApproaches.result: The mechanism accepts an exclusive toll concession.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Receive bounded recurring toll income; poorer households lose access and a named grievance can follow.

bosses.objective: Restore, monopolize or disable the crossing; a battle victory grants access but does not restore rescue service.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Watch That Never Ends
bosses.mechanic: The watch points at the greatest party ward and removes up to 6, remembering only what it actually took. On its next action the stolen light becomes a piercing blow at the same ally. Sacred interruption discards that stolen charge.

phase.change: Its lost patrol appears as an 8-point ward, not extra untargetable combatants. The next theft is announced a turn earlier.
phase.telegraph: Rain fills six empty helmets, and their lamps gather around the remaining watcher.

bosses.biography: This was the last keeper at a signal tower the commander ordered dark. Their spouse reached the locked refuge door after the bell stopped. The watcher now takes lights from armored travelers, unable to bear seeing a lamp carried safely past the place where theirs failed.
bosses.rumor: Travelers lose lamp oil beside the abandoned signal tower. A widower keeps a second wick burning there and says the wind sometimes speaks the old password.

noncombatApproaches.label: Complete one night of the abandoned watch
prerequisites: Identify the surviving widower rather than an invented witness
noncombatApproaches.result: The widower lights the second wick and the watcher relinquishes its stolen lamps.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The crossing gets a remembered night watch; the dead keeper is released, not recruited.

noncombatApproaches.label: Return the seized household lanterns
noncombatApproaches.result: A returning chain of lights leads the watcher home.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Families remember the restitution; no stolen coin is kept.

noncombatApproaches.label: Bind the apparition to your own toll post
noncombatApproaches.result: A coerced ward protects your holding for a bounded season.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Break an existing mercy oath; a named witness creates local evidence if present, and the ward ends unless renewed.

bosses.objective: Release, repay or bind the abandoned watch; victory recovers stolen light without establishing an ongoing service.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Captain Without a Shore
bosses.mechanic: The captain marks a caster with rising water and orders its drowned crew to pull that ally under. Defending breaks the mark; removing a crew member reduces the next undertow bonus. The captain cannot regenerate a destroyed crew.

phase.change: A ship bell removes the captain's remaining ward and adds one final, visibly charged undertow pulse. Interrupting the bell cancels the pulse.
phase.telegraph: Its mouth opens around a dry bell; even the dead crew steps away.

bosses.biography: A Saltreach privateer sold the captain's safe-harbor promise to two rival fleets. When both attacked, the captain scuttled the ship rather than surrender the youngest crew. It now returns with everyone it tried to save, demanding a berth from descendants who do not know which old promise they inherited.
bosses.rumor: On the lowest tide an unregistered crew asks for a berth. An old rope-maker claims the ship sank deliberately, but has never seen who stood at its helm.

noncombatApproaches.label: Find the lost shore and lay the crew to rest
prerequisites: Locate an actual coast burial landing
noncombatApproaches.result: The captain brings the crew ashore for a final farewell.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The night berth reopens; families can dispute the captain choice in later conversations.

noncombatApproaches.label: Give the returned ship a lawful night berth
prerequisites: Negotiate with the current harbor authority
noncombatApproaches.result: The undead crew accepts limited night passage without taking living passengers.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: A named harbor agreement changes night trade, while regional corpse/curse law still applies.

noncombatApproaches.label: Hire the captain for forbidden crossings
noncombatApproaches.result: The ship provides one discreet passage contract.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Earn smuggling opportunities and local pursuit if a witness identifies the cargo.

bosses.objective: Resolve the crew berth, grant limited service or use a dangerous smuggling route; victory only clears the current harbor threat.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Glass-Tide Witness
bosses.mechanic: The many-eyed creature targets the party strongest spell, but opens a soft pupil while aiming. A physical strike through a marked pupil cancels its precision bonus. Magic still damages it normally and is never wholly invalidated.

phase.change: Its glass shell cracks: gain one temporary 5-point ward from the fragments and alternate caster aim with a lower-power party pulse.
phase.telegraph: The sea-facing lens splits; smaller eyes turn toward every moving hand.

bosses.biography: A moon watcher raised it in a silver bowl to show their missing lover whatever shore they had reached. The lover returned old and almost blind; the watcher refused to let the reflection close. The witness keeps collecting faces, trying to find the one expression the watcher remembered before the years changed it.
bosses.rumor: The tide shrine bowl shows visitors one summer younger. A fish seller says a returned sailor refuses to look into it, even though their own lover tended it for years.

noncombatApproaches.label: Let the returned sailor choose a final reflection
noncombatApproaches.result: A chosen farewell closes the collection of faces.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The sailor remains an independent contact; no de-aging or involuntary sacrifice is claimed.

noncombatApproaches.label: Redirect its lens toward an empty tide chamber
noncombatApproaches.result: The creature studies a repeating tide instead of living faces.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The shrine gains a bounded forecasting service; the creature remains alive below it.

noncombatApproaches.label: Keep a lens for your own scrying
prerequisites: Extract a complete lens after inspecting the shell
noncombatApproaches.result: Gain a bounded scrying relic from the broken collection.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Learn one regional lead; the returned sailor distrusts you and the relic cannot reveal private secrets without later evidence.

bosses.objective: Free the collected reflections, redirect their gaze or take a limited scrying relic; victory does not restore anyone youth.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Unfinished Son
bosses.mechanic: The casting closes its metal plates for a heavy blow, but the seam made by the missing arm is visible. A blunt counter or lightning removes the charged bonus. Its ward never exceeds the amount advertised.

phase.change: The old furnace brace breaks. It loses 2 armor and gains 3 power on one announced last charge; later actions return to its ordinary cycle.
phase.telegraph: The unfinished arm falls away, exposing the casting seam.

bosses.biography: A Highstone smith cast a substitute for a son lost in the upper mine. They left one hand unfinished because the boy had always wanted to choose a trade of his own. The casting now guards the cold furnace, furious that each apprentice is sent into the same mountain before being allowed a different life.
bosses.rumor: The furnace guard wears a child-sized glove over one enormous hand. An elderly apprentice says the maker never meant to finish that hand.

noncombatApproaches.label: Give the unfinished hand a chosen purpose
noncombatApproaches.result: Fit a rescue tool rather than a weapon; the casting helps maintain mine shelters.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Improve a real pass safety service and preserve the son separate mortal history.

noncombatApproaches.label: Close the unsafe shaft and move the apprentices
noncombatApproaches.result: The guard allows the furnace to relight after the apprentices move safely.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Ore supply is reduced for one season; safety and apprentice relationships improve.

noncombatApproaches.label: Sell the casting to a war patron
noncombatApproaches.result: The patron removes the casting and pays 60 gold.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The furnace opens, but a named military beneficiary receives the guard; later war harm can return as a callback.

bosses.objective: Change the casting purpose, make the mine safe or sell its power; combat defeat dismantles the current guard rather than resurrecting its maker's son.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Furnace Widow
bosses.mechanic: The dragon visibly fills its chest before a fire breath. Ice or disruption cancels an unfinished breath; defending reduces the completed wave. After breathing, the throat remains exposed to one marked hit.

phase.change: It curls around its last egg, gaining 6 ward and replacing alternate breaths with a narrower, stronger bite at the closest protector. The egg is scenery with explicit story stakes, not an untargetable damage source.
phase.telegraph: One wing closes around a stone-grey egg; the next inhale stops halfway.

bosses.biography: Highstone furnace masters bought heat from the dragon's mate and failed to bring the final winter food. After the mate died, the widow nested in the warmth of their abandoned foundry with the last unhatched egg. It raids convoys because the mountain has too little prey left to feed both the nest and the households beneath it.
bosses.rumor: Every stolen convoy loses meat but keeps its ore. A shepherd has heard a smaller heartbeat beneath the foundry roar.

noncombatApproaches.label: Arrange a finite winter food covenant
prerequisites: Find willing suppliers with actual stock
noncombatApproaches.result: The widow stops raiding this route for one bounded season.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Food stock falls; named suppliers and protected travelers remember the cost.

noncombatApproaches.label: Prepare a warmer nest away from the convoy road
prerequisites: Find an actual sheltered mountain chamber
noncombatApproaches.result: The dragon moves the egg after verifying the new chamber warmth.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Restore the route and gain no dragon mount or immortal army.

noncombatApproaches.label: Steal the egg and bargain from concealment
noncombatApproaches.result: Gain the named egg as a dangerous unique property; the widow abandons trade raids to hunt for it.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Open a lucrative patron sale or ransom, create pursuit tied to actual discovery, and strain compassionate traits.

bosses.objective: Feed, relocate, exploit or drive away the nest; battle victory clears a route without automatically killing or looting the egg.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Mother of Empty Nests
bosses.mechanic: The sovereign shelters a sprout before regenerating. A fire hit or broken root ward cancels one heal. Defeating the sprout ends shared regeneration and triggers one visibly announced grieving wave, never an infinite replacement.

phase.change: Its abandoned nests fall open: reduce ward by 4 and allow a one-time thorn wave. Party wards and guard reduce that wave.
phase.telegraph: The crown parts and every empty nest tilts toward the party.

bosses.biography: This Blackgrove guardian grew around the nests of creatures driven out by a timber contract. It learned the sound of hungry children and allowed refugees to gather deadwood. When a patron sold their children young birds as ornaments, the guardian closed the same path to everyone, including the households it once sheltered.
bosses.rumor: The living gate opens for a child carrying an empty cage. A logger insists the guardian once let their family through.

noncombatApproaches.label: Return the surviving caged birds
noncombatApproaches.result: The sovereign opens a narrow household path and keeps the deeper nesting ground closed.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: A named seller loses illicit stock; families gain a safe deadwood route.

noncombatApproaches.label: Build a shared deadwood and nesting boundary
prerequisites: Negotiate with the current logging households
noncombatApproaches.result: A marked gathering boundary lets households live without taking the remaining nests.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Seasonal timber supply drops slightly; local safety improves.

noncombatApproaches.label: Force the nesting ground into your timber holding
noncombatApproaches.result: Receive a bounded timber concession after driving the guardian back.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Profit through lost nesting habitat; named refugees and keepers can oppose the holding.

bosses.objective: Restore a nesting bargain, reserve a limited route or profit from the grove loss; winning a fight alone does not replenish timber or birds.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Orchard Wife
bosses.mechanic: The witch wears a false likeness as a visible ward and strikes through the surviving illusion. Inspecting removes its false ward before the strike; ordinary ward and armor still protect her real body.

phase.change: She abandons the likeness and uses one seeded orchard charm: a small fear wave, followed by ordinary weakening strikes. No new ancestry or portrait identity is assigned.
phase.telegraph: The young reflected face stays smiling while the real woman begins to weep.

bosses.biography: The Orchard Wife kept a lover alive through a winter by grafting their breath into trees. Years later the lover begged to leave, but she continued speaking to the orchard as though every bloom was an answer. Now she buys names from passing travelers, trying to find a person who will choose the old life willingly rather than be trapped in it.
bosses.rumor: An orchard flowers on the coldest night, but its owner charges a visitor their childhood nickname. A former lover says the trees still answer in their voice.

noncombatApproaches.label: Help the former lover reclaim their own breath
prerequisites: Learn which tree holds their chosen graft
noncombatApproaches.result: The graft is released with the lover present; the orchard loses its unnatural winter bloom.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The witch survives and can resent or later accept the loss; ordinary fruit returns by season.

noncombatApproaches.label: Offer another source of winter heat
prerequisites: Work with a forge priest or practiced craft companion
noncombatApproaches.result: A plain heated shelter replaces the need to purchase names.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Maintain one household garden service, with periodic fuel costs and no compelled lover.

noncombatApproaches.label: Buy the stored names for a private broker
prerequisites: Decide which identified names are being transferred
noncombatApproaches.result: Receive a finite payment of 55 gold and a broker contact.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The affected named travelers may discover the sale; secrecy is determined by witnesses rather than automatic omniscience.

bosses.objective: End, replace or exploit the orchard bargain; battle victory ends its immediate attack without deciding the lover's relationship.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Saltless Captain
bosses.mechanic: The captain grants company ward, names a volley target and commands a coordinated strike. A surrendered or defeated supporter lowers the volley bonus; the captain cannot command a captive to act.

phase.change: One frightened conscript publicly asks to surrender. Offer a real battle capture/surrender opportunity; refusing leaves the regular volley cycle. The captain gains no free attack from the scene.
phase.telegraph: A conscript lowers their weapon and looks toward the well instead of the banner.

bosses.biography: An Ashplain border officer was promised water for families that sheltered the garrison. The supply caravan was diverted to a claimant's coronation, and the officer began charging every well for the lost shipment. Their company now controls water that once belonged to the very households they claim to protect.
bosses.rumor: The well guards demand silver but carry empty salt sacks. One frightened soldier asks whether a caravan carrying drinking water ever reached the coronation.

noncombatApproaches.label: Recover the diverted water and bring it to the families
prerequisites: Complete a supply escort or negotiated return
noncombatApproaches.result: The company lowers the levy after witnessing the water delivered.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: A bounded well service reopens; the captain must still face any existing named charges.

noncombatApproaches.label: Pay willing conscripts to leave the company
noncombatApproaches.result: The captain loses enough supporters to accept a limited surrender.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Named soldiers leave independently; no permanent companion is granted without a later recruitment agreement.

noncombatApproaches.label: Take over the well levy with the claimant's seal
prerequisites: Choose a charter or coerced arrangement
noncombatApproaches.result: Gain the water concession and finite initial income.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Well prices rise, affected households remember the beneficiary, and regional law can respond to witnessed coercion.

bosses.objective: Return water, release the company, capture the captain or control the levy; killing the company is only one approach.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Crown Beneath the Ash
bosses.mechanic: The king transfers existing retainer ward into its crown, then makes a charged regal strike. Interrupt the transfer, defeat the ward lender or strip the crown to reduce the strike. Health and ward are never invented from a dead retainer.

phase.change: The crown exposes a broken family seal. The king makes one last announced party pulse, then loses its ability to take retainer ward.
phase.telegraph: The crown tilts and a small family sign appears beneath the royal metal.

bosses.biography: An Ashplain king ordered a refuge burned because its free hearth undermined his claimant fire. His own youngest child was hiding there with a lover from the defeated house. He rises whenever a new coronation beacon is lit, searching for a family he destroyed while insisting his kingdom must still be grateful.
bosses.rumor: The returned crown turns away from children singing a refuge song. A charcoal seller says the same song was forbidden at the last living coronation.

noncombatApproaches.label: Bring the lost refuge song and the child surviving token
noncombatApproaches.result: The king recognizes the loss and relinquishes its borrowed crown.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The beacon can become a free hearth; descendants choose their own account of the old dynasty.

noncombatApproaches.label: End the returning coronation through a public rival settlement
noncombatApproaches.result: A new political settlement stops the old beacon summons.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: A named living ruler gains legitimacy; neither ancestral guilt nor automatic loyalty is imposed on descendants.

noncombatApproaches.label: Use the crown to enforce your own claim
prerequisites: Choose an actual holding to receive the claim
noncombatApproaches.result: Gain one bounded legitimacy or intimidation advantage in that holding.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: A coerced claimant benefits; mercy oath and remembered household losses can oppose the bargain.

bosses.objective: Resolve the king's loss, replace its political summons or exploit the crown; victory dismantles this returning claim, not every later war.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Listener at the Drowned Door
bosses.mechanic: The listener seals only the last used damaging technique for one round; another attack, support move or cleanse remains available. It follows the seal with a protective ward, then a lower party pulse.

phase.change: The lost room begins repeating the last technique twice. Keep the same one-round seal cap; increase ward by 4, then expose a seam when the repeat ends.
phase.telegraph: Two voices repeat one word, but neither can say anything new.

bosses.biography: Before Bellwater changed its river course, a grandparent kept an evening story room beside the crossing school. The flood took the room while the grandparent was searching for a child who had already escaped. The listening spirit repeats the last words spoken at its drowned door, hoping the next voice will tell it what happened after the water.
bosses.rumor: Below the crossing school a door repeats the last sentence spoken above it. A grown boat-builder refuses to finish the bedtime story they learned there.

noncombatApproaches.label: Bring the escaped child grown account
noncombatApproaches.result: The listener hears the survival it could not witness and lets the room fall silent.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: A named living person keeps their own history; the school gains the story without pretending the grandparent returned alive.

noncombatApproaches.label: Build an ordinary story room above the flood line
noncombatApproaches.result: Children gather in a new room while the old spirit hears them through the open doorway.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Gain a bounded school/community service with ongoing upkeep.

noncombatApproaches.label: Sell the repeating-door technique to an academy patron
prerequisites: Record the mechanism without claiming fresh testimony
noncombatApproaches.result: A named patron buys the copied mechanism for 40 gold.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The original listener remains unresolved; the boat-builder can resent the profitable copy.

bosses.objective: Complete a remembered story, build a living room or profit from an unresolved echo; victory gives access to the drowned room without a living witness.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

bosses.name: The Guest Who Would Not Leave
bosses.mechanic: The guest sets an empty cup for an injured undead ally, then drains a living party member to fill it. A ward reduces actual transferred health; sacred disruption breaks the cup before the transfer.

phase.change: The guest turns the meal inward: its next transfer can heal itself only, with a 6-health cap. Subsequent turns return to the same advertised cycle.
phase.telegraph: The empty place at the table is suddenly its own.

bosses.biography: A Bellwater burial host refused to close the annual table after their daughter died far from the river. When every other guest aged and stopped returning, the host kept places for their bodies as well as their names. It now takes warmth from living visitors, convinced that an unfinished meal means no one has truly left.
bosses.rumor: The burial feast serves cold food but leaves guests feverish. A ferryman says one cup at its table has never been touched, even by the dead.

noncombatApproaches.label: Bring the daughter's chosen last message and empty her cup
prerequisites: Find a dated message through the actual ferry route
Hear its stated farewell without inventing a new voice
noncombatApproaches.result: The host closes the meal and lets the dead guests leave.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: A normal yearly memorial remains, while no new feeding donor or resurrected companion is created.

noncombatApproaches.label: Replace the stolen warmth with a living household feast
noncombatApproaches.result: The host attends one bounded memorial without draining a living guest.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: Family stress falls modestly; the feast must not become an automatic eternal cure.

noncombatApproaches.label: Take the guest's cups for a predatory patron
prerequisites: Meet a patron who values the cups
Choose whether the theft is concealed or witnessed
noncombatApproaches.result: Receive 50 gold and a dangerous named relic lead.
noncombatApproaches.consequence: The feast disperses violently; surviving living guests can identify the theft and regional charges follow actual observation.

bosses.objective: Finish, replace or exploit the meal; combat victory ends the drain but does not automatically reconcile the surviving family.
bosses.presentation: A complete existing-species portrait, with a stable saved boss identity. Named scene illustration is a later art task; do not relabel a different species portrait.

implementationAssumptions.speciesIds: Exact48 ENEMY_SPECIES row IDs from baseline enemies.js; no separate ENEMY_SPECIES_IDS export exists.
implementationAssumptions.weaknessNormalization: The asset uses sacred; the existing combat engine uses radiance. Normalize sacred to radiance at integration. physical is a new explicit category; it must not mean every old basic attack gets an unexplained bonus.
implementationAssumptions.patterns: Only requested pattern names are used. Species pattern is the base; personality modifies cadence/power without replacing species biology.
implementationAssumptions.cadence: cycle is ordered design data, not executable engine code. amount on damage actions is a bounded bonus/penalty relative to the encounter base power; ward/heal/drain amounts are absolute maxima. All conditional actions need explicit fallback to an ordinary strike or small ward.
implementationAssumptions.targets: Selector names such as largest_current_magic/last_attacker are proposed bounded hooks. Invalid/dead targets reselect a living legal target; no attack may act through a captured/dead enemy.
implementationAssumptions.resistances: Resistance here means the status is wholly rejected with clear feedback. Bleed/poison resistance is present on every currently bloodless species; fear depends on remaining personhood, while burn depends on material.
implementationAssumptions.newStatuses: poison,fear,prey marks,charge seals and technique seals require turn durations, cleansing, visible descriptions and saved-state validation. No permanent trait or attribute mutation.
implementationAssumptions.bosses: Twelve original named encounters, two per real region. Biography, rumor and solution text are authored assets only. Root must implement scene prerequisites, attended costs, named contacts, bounded services and consequences before displaying a playable promise.
implementationAssumptions.geography: requiredTags is proposed suitability metadata derived from actual terrain/site/services and remembered scene facts. It must not fabricate a coast, harbor, mine, shrine faith or living witness to satisfy a template. Missing settings require a different encounter or explicit copied-account presentation.
implementationAssumptions.compatibility: Snapshot the accepted encounter plan, phase state, identities and proof. Genuine old pending battles/quests retain their existing actors/turns/resources/actions. Never migrate a completed old encounter into a new unsatisfied objective.
implementationAssumptions.portraitBindings: Reuse only exact species art for this design pass. Distinct portrait cells alone are not counted as distinct tactical archetypes. Named art and age/curse variants remain separate production tasks.
